key_insight: This paper introduces a "living" benchmark that can automatically generate evaluation questions and answers for information retrieval from electronic health records, making benchmark creation faster and easier to keep up to date.
problem_solved: It addresses the problem that existing EHR benchmark datasets for LLM-based clinical assistants are manually curated, expensive to maintain, and quickly become outdated as clinical workflows and model capabilities change.
method: Automatically generates question-answer pairs from electronic health record data
Uses a scalable framework to refresh benchmark content over time
Supports ongoing evaluation of clinical information retrieval systems in a way that adapts to new records and evolving needs
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this enables more realistic and continuously updated evaluation of clinical assistant systems. It can improve safety, reliability, and long-term benchmarking for healthcare NLP and retrieval models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing EHR data flowing into automated QA generation
Before/after comparison of static benchmarks vs. living benchmarks
Icon set for EHR records, LLM assistant, and evaluation metrics
Timeline graphic showing continuous benchmark updates over time
paper_title: A Living Benchmark for Information Retrieval from Electronic Health Records
paper_authors: Jordan L. Cahoon, Chloe O. Stanwyck, Sulaiman Somani, Philip Chung, Kevin R Keet
